lesson: [lfm2_24b_a2b] Expert pools found by the attribution-plus-exclusion recipe passed where single experts and raw routing failed. The recipe: sweep single-layer blocks, scan one layer for attribution and routing, take the target's top 6-14 experts, and drop any expert attributed to a collateral skill (weekday, chinese_numeral, digit writers). Passes: L37 12-expert facts pool (-.21), L30 8-expert roman pool (-.407), L30 6-expert SVA pool (-.232), L13 6-expert month pool (-.518, weekday .076).

[lfm2_24b_a2b] The single-expert routing leaders did nothing alone. L22 e43 (code routing 160) dropped code by -.004 and L26 e22 (math routing 129) dropped math by -.004. Code stayed at or below .07 even for 8-expert code-routed pools at L33/L39, and multilingual and en_fr never localized. Don't spend screens on code/multilingual expert sets on this model.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Logit-lens reading of w2 found real numeric writers that are shared across skills, so they can't pass a single-skill screen. L39 e63/e53/e21 have 9.9x/6.2x/4.3x digit-direction energy; ablating them hit math .133 and the roman digit control .73. L38 e36 cut math .63 but also chinese .96. L33 e12 alone equals the whole L33 block (month .87, weekday .70, math .34).

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Clean search-split pools still fail when the effect sits on one key expert that random same-size sets often contain. The L31 weekday pool dropped .575 but a random set dropped .605 (e12 inside). The L9 month pool (.386) and L20 month pool (.30) lost to random sets at .576 and .335. Check that the target drop clearly exceeds the drop of the single strongest expert.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Attention head groups were almost always too broad. L38 h1/9/12/14 and h12/14/17/18/23/24 broke nearly every skill (facts .96). L30 facts heads [21,3,29,26,5] dropped facts .396 but failed because general_text (.222) counts as an other skill. Early heads (L2/L10/L14/L18) pulled in month and weekday at .5 to .9.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Skills with tiny bases (chinese_numeral .033, weekday control .004, SVA control .036) produce huge relative swings that block screens. Random blocks dropped chinese up to .975, and controls moved by -0.9 to -4. The define_skill cap (8) was already used, so plan new skills with high bases and stable controls early.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Attribution-plus-exclusion expert pools passed the screen 27 times out of 30 (3-7 experts per layer). The recipe: take one layer's top attribution experts for the target skill and drop any expert with attribution on weekday, month, a_an or facts. Caveat: 17 of the 27 passes are chinese_numeral, whose base is only .033, so their huge relative drops (.235-.89) rest on very few correct items. The month pools (8 passes, .186-.426, controls within ±.05) and the L7/L8 antonym pools (.344/.359) are the trustworthy results.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Splitting a leaky pool often rescued it. L7 month and chinese pools each leaked antonym (.451/.321). Splitting them isolated L7 [23,46,42,38], which passed for antonym at .344. The L3 month pool lost its antonym leak (.221) once e2/e26/e32 were removed: [4,8,15] passed at .241. Removing routing-identified e28 from the L2 month pool removed an en_fr leak of .21, and [62,37,30] passed at .361.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Routing selectivity predicted a causal part only in early layers. L8 e14/e25/e17 (14.7/7.7/5.6x antonym routing) passed at .359. Late routing leaders did nothing when ablated (all ≤ .035): antonym L13 e29 (63x), L22 e37 (50x), L20/L23/L27/L30 pairs; code L33 e55 (89x); multilingual L38 e20 (82x) and L34 e6 (33x); math L33 e49 (18.5x). Attribution scores for antonym were near zero everywhere even where ablation showed real effects.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Weight-only logit-lens reading did not localize skills. L39 experts with 6-17x energy along the unembedding directions for Arabic, CJK and Cyrillic (e22, e9, e16, e48), or for code tokens (e33, e29, e50), moved multilingual and code by at most .06 when ablated. Every single-layer block I tested was broad; L38 breaks everything.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Month families of 16-64 neurons grown at L0/L1 from seeds 10044 and 5788 always dropped weekday by .46-.53 as well as month by .6-.68. That held even with max-cosine penalties against weekday units, so these are shared calendar-name units. Month head groups at L6, L22 and L26 (drops .54-.6) also dropped weekday .27-.54. Weekday's control base is .004, and SVA and a_an controls swing by ±.4-.9. Plan high-base skills with stable controls before the define_skill cap (8) is used up.

On LFM2-24B-A2B (tied embeddings), per-expert down-projection energy on a token category's unembedding rows (times embedding_norm), relative to random tokens, predicted real parts. The largest outlier worked even as a single expert: L31 e12 had 5.0x weekday energy and dropped weekday_successor .607 with random draws at 0. Broad categories needed 16-22 experts from one late layer. Country+capital writers passed for facts at L37 (16 experts, .183), L35 (20, .173) and L36 (22, .154). French/Spanish/German function-word writers at L38 (16) passed en_fr_translation at .173 with control .003.

The same per-expert energies also find the leaking member of a set. The L36 geo set of 16 had a .234 weekday leak; dropping e47, its highest-weekday-energy member, removed the leak. e47 plus the next two weekday writers (e11, e3) then passed for weekday at .24 with control -.005. Grow a set step by step (8->12->16 gave facts .143->.17->.183) and swap members until every other skill is under max(.05, target/3).

Math and code would not localise to single-layer expert sets in this top-4-routed MoE. The tries that moved nothing (all <=.035) were digit writers at L35-39 with 3-6x digit energy, math-routed experts (L26 e22 134x enrichment, L18, L14), code-routed experts (L22 e43 150x, L33 e14/55) and 16-expert sets picked from the unembedding or router rows. The only big math drops came from hubs that also wrecked other skills: L33 e12 (math .34, month .87, weekday .70) and L38 e36 (math .60, chinese_numeral .97).

Router-row x token-embedding z-scores were good at nominating candidates but rarely causal on their own. Country-routed sets of 4-5 experts (L30 e8 z 2.5, L31 e56 z 2.34, L36 e18 z 2.5) dropped facts <=.03. L23 e1, the most weekday-routed expert (z 2.09), improved weekday by .18 when ablated. Use routing as a second line of evidence next to write energy.

Several part kinds failed in ways worth avoiding. Attention head groups of 4, even when picked by attribution (L2, L30 KV group 0, L38), damaged 5+ skills at once. Blocks L33 and L37 were not selective (L37: facts .338 but roman .556). Expert sets in L39 always caused broad collateral. 128-unit dense-MLP clusters at L0 gave noisy mixed effects. Low-base skills such as chinese_numeral (base .033) and a_an_article swing a lot with random parts (random draws up to .18), so passes on them are weak evidence.

Facts below L35 seems more spread out. An L31 country/capital set of 24 experts reached .159 on the search half and stayed clean (others <=.038), but failed the held-out check. Marginal drops near the .15 threshold are risky; aim for >=.18 before screening.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Number-token subspace energy in expert down-projections predicted the one real math part. L39 expert 63 had 8x the median energy in the digit/round-number unembedding subspace, and its top direction writes 30/20/50/25/40. Ablating L39 [63,22,58,53] dropped math .281 while random same-size parts dropped about 0. It still failed the screen because chinese_numeral, another skill that outputs numbers, dropped .132 against a .094 limit. Without e63, math fell to .096. Don't run two built-in or agent skills that both output Arabic numbers.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] A huge attribution score on one expert often marks a generic hub. L38 e36 had math attribution .277 (20x the next unit) and chinese_numeral .743, and its top direction writes <|startoftext|>/<|im_start|>. Ablated with e38 and e3 it dropped math .65, chinese_numeral .95 and roman_numeral's control .98. Read the logit lens before building a set around the top-attributed expert.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Clean writer experts in the weights were inert when ablated (drops under .03). Examples: L33 e14 writes '(' (code z=7), L36 e2 writes la/une, L37 e53 writes au/à, L38 e18 writes d'/l', the code-router experts at L15, and number writers at L34/L35 that also matched math attribution. In this MoE, only the last layer (L39) had expert sets that bottleneck a skill. Code and French look spread across many experts.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Digit-copy scores on attention value/output weights (layers 2, 6, ..., 38) found strong heads that turned out to be shared hubs. L30 GQA group 6 (heads 24-27, h24 score 3.69) dropped math .585 but also roman .957, month .952 and weekday .806. L38 heads 0/2/8/11 (scores about 5) together dropped math .205, while either GQA group alone dropped it only about .05, so the heads are redundant.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Early-layer experts with high a_an_article attribution (L5 e34 1.07, L10 e25 .76) dropped the target about .8, but also dropped its own control .9-.97 and moved antonym/month/weekday by .3-.5. A large attribution score on a low-base skill (base .15) often means general-text disruption. Check that the control is stable before screening.

Plan the 8 agent-skill slots ahead of time. The cap was already full, so I couldn't define a number-word-to-digits skill to test the L39 number writers without the chinese_numeral clash. Keep 1-2 slots free for skills that the weight reading suggests mid-run.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Measuring each expert's w2 energy inside the digit-unembedding subspace (top 8 SVD dims) found clear digit-writer experts in late layers. L35 expert 49 scored 0.026 against a 0.004 baseline, L37 experts 23 and 27 about 0.032, and L32 experts 8, 11 and 22 about 0.01. Ablating them barely moved math: L35 [4,46,49,61,63] 0.004 and L32 [8,10,11,22,60,61] 0.009. So in this MoE, single-layer digit-writer sets do not bottleneck math.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] Router-gate reading (ffn_norm-scaled embeddings @ gate.weight.T, top-4 routing frequency per token category) gave sharp digit routing in L2-L5: L3 expert 30 gets 80% of digit tokens and 0% of other categories, L2 expert 20 gets 80%. Code, French, German and English tokens gave weak selectivity (at most about 0.1-0.3), so this probe works for closed classes like digits but not for broad skills.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] The early digit-routed experts at L3 [13,17,30,37,52] dropped month_successor by 0.161 and weekday_successor by 0.149 but left math unchanged (-0.006). The controls swung hugely (antonym control -0.68, chinese_numeral control -1.29). Ablating them also shifted other skills by up to 0.15, so the effect is broad and unselective; I spent no screen on it.

[lfm2_24b_a2b] The L5 digit-routed experts [7,18,20,24,49] improved chinese_numeral by 0.40 (drop -0.402) rather than hurting it, which suggests digit and Chinese-numeral routes compete. Large negative drops like this are a cue to look for competing pathways, not a reason to screen the part.

General: math (base 0.82) was not dented by any 5-6 expert set I tried in layers 3-35. For broad, high-margin skills on 64-expert MoE models, test multi-layer blocks or larger cross-layer expert unions first, and check the skill's base margin before spending ablations on lexical writer experts.
